tldr: The transported point-density likelihood has an exact two-scale expansion: a source likelihood term of order \(n^{-2/5}\) plus \(d_a(\widehat q-q)\). The source terms converge to independent curved-density invelope laws. The target sample contributes one shared binomial Gaussian, so \(m/n^{4/5}\to\kappa\) is the elbow between source-dominated and target-dominated inference. Zero arm or contrast sensitivities retain the source scale even for a small target sample. A finite observable connected interval has pointwise limiting coverage \(0.90\) for every diverging source and target sequence, with length of order \(n^{-2/5}+|d_1-d_0|m^{-1/2}\). Nearby mixtures need not be globally log-concave. The law properties, estimator and causal target remain unchanged.

The benchmark's quantitative envelopes, binary probability bounds, distributional transport and critical ratio are maintained restrictions, not assumptions attributed to those published theorems. The general projection domain is a weaker boundary comparator requiring only finite first moment and nondegenerate support.
